title: Edge buffer ratchet notes — 2029-03-22
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick midweek notes from the small-capacity working huddle. Focused on the edge buffer ratchet experiment (new terminology vs `priming`) — trying a smaller, faster ramp-up of reserve slots in three test regions for 48h. This doc captures what we saw, immediate triage, and concrete follow-ups for oncall and provisioning teams.

Attendees (ad-hoc): Aisha (lead), Diego (ops), Hannah (scheduling+instrumentation), Marcus (allocator), Priya (cost controls) — pinged via #infra-edge and #oncall-runbook.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Experiment: rapid buffer ratchet in ORD, AMS, and SIN for H100 pools; goal: reduce cold-start latency tail by pre-creating 5-10 lightweight slots per AZ and tearing down if idle > 30m.
- Result: median cold-start latency improved ~18% in ORD and AMS, minimal improvement in SIN (noisy preemption and VN failures).
- Cost delta: short-lived increase (~+2.1% token-hour cost for test window); projected steady-state +0.6% if we keep current idle timeout.
- Key issue: SIN encountered autoscaler loop with preemptible reclaim events — leads to flapping and higher billing due to frequent re-allocs.

Notes / observations:
- ORD (us-east-2-ish): toggled ratchet to 8 reserve slots across 2 AZs at 03:00 UTC 2029-03-21. Observed fewer 503s during 04:00–07:00 spike. Cold-start p95 reduced from 380ms -> 310ms for common model variants (redwood-13B-q4f).
- AMS (europe-west-1-ish): similar config, ratchet 6 slots, saw steady p90 improvement and smoother queueing. No allocator churn.
- SIN (ap-southeast-1-ish): ratchet target 6 slots, but preemptible nodes reclaimed rapidly (GCP spot-like), causing allocator to rebind GPUs repeatedly. End-to-end latency for affected requests worsened in two AZs.
- KV-cache warmup: prefix cache priming appears effective — endpoints with persistent prefixes show best improvements. However, for short-chat flows the benefit is small.
- Billing telemetry: short window sampling shows an increase in instance-hours but token-cost amortization improved slightly because fewer retries and fewer long-tail retries. Need better simulation to extrapolate monthly cost.

Debug traces and artifacts we collected:
- Allocator logs: PR #814 (allocator/rate-limiter tweak) added a backoff that reduced cross-AZ rescheduling; Marcus to follow up with a patch to reduce aggressive reschedule on flapping nodes.
- SRE traces: linked trace ids: TRACE-20290321-ORD-44, TRACE-20290321-AMS-18, TRACE-20290321-SIN-07 (captured in the trace-archive).
- Grafana dashboards updated: edge-buffer/ratchet-experiment-2029-03-21 (Hannah).

Immediate action items (owners + due dates):
- Marcus: revert overly-aggressive rebind after preemptible reclaim (allocator config). Target: soft-disable rebind for preemptible flag until additional stability gating is in. Due: 2029-03-24. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/814.
- Hannah: add a SIN-specific probe (synthetic cold-start requests every 15m across AZs) to better capture flapping. Due: 2029-03-25. Add to dashboards and alert rule.
- Diego: add a temporary guard in the autoscaler to avoid immediate scale-in if nodes show >2 reclaims in 60m. Due: 2029-03-23. Ticket: INFRA-3421.
- Priya: run a quick cost sensitivity scenario — simulate steady-state ratchet with idle timeout 15m, 30m, 60m and provide expected monthly delta. Due: 2029-03-28.
- Aisha: draft an RFC-lite describing ratchet lifecycle (when to ramp, how to tie to SLOs) and send it to eng-infra/legal for export-control sanity (we're touching region-level allocation). Due: 2029-04-01.

Open questions / discussion notes:
- Should ratchet be AZ-local or region-wide? Observed benefit when AZ-local (keeps caches more effective) but cost of fragmentation may increase. Need simulation.
- How to coordinate ratchet with Dedicated reserved pools? If a customer has pinned slots, ratchet must not attempt to pre-empt those. Need stronger tenant isolation checks in allocator.
- Preemptible behavior differs wildly by cloud/region — should we maintain per-region policies (SIN more conservative)? Likely yes.
- Is the 30m idle timeout the right default? We saw good perf at 30m, but costs scale. 15m may be a sweet spot in high-throughput areas.

Incidents and postmortem notes:
- SIN flapping: short incident window (2029-03-21 09:12–09:47 UTC) where autoscaler loops led to higher-than-normal cost and elevated error rate for ~1.6% of requests. Root cause: preemptible reclaim + allocator rebind policy. Severity: Sev2. Current mitigation: manual disable ratchet in SIN and applied temporary scale-in guard. Follow-up: full allocator config change (Marcus).

Ideas / brainstorm (rough):
- Adaptive ratchet: use short-term prediction (5–15m) from traffic model to only spin up reserve slots when probability of cold-starts > threshold. Would reduce cost for low-traffic windows. (Hannah + Marcus to prototype).
- Hybrid reserve: combine small hot pool (0.5–1 GPU reserved for immediate small requests) + larger light-weight pool for queued cold starts to spread cost. Needs allocator/serve-runtime coordination.

Runbook edits (todo):
- Add SIN-specific note in 'edge-buffering-runbook-v3' warning about preemptible reclaim sensitivity.
- Clarify when oncall should toggle ratchet (current doc ambiguous).
- Add a quick checklist for disabling ratchet per-region and steps to re-enable safely.

Meeting logistics / next check-in:
- We will run the ratchet in ORD+AMS for another 72h with updated allocator backoff and autoscaler guard. Re-evaluate on Fri 2029-03-25 15:00 UTC in short sync (15m).
- Marcus & Hannah to own the data ingest for that sync; Diego will be oncall for quick toggles.

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep language away from `priming` in customer-facing docs; call out as `reserve ratchet` or `edge reserve` to avoid confusion with prewarming.
- Follow up with platform-eng on how to expose reserve health in per-customer dashboards.

Raw snippets / quick logs (copied):
- "alloc: bind node n-348 -> slot s-992, preemptible=true, reclaims=3 -> backoff applied"
- "probe: synthetic coldcall ord-az1 p95 310ms vs baseline 380ms"

References / links: see linked_artifacts above and internal dash: grafana/edge-buffer/ratchet-experiment-2029-03-21

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally terse. Will draft a fuller experiment postmortem if we keep ratchet enabled beyond the next 72h. For now, focus: avoid SIN churn and validate allocator backoff improvements.

-- Aisha
